function: p. 3: DDPG and Double-DDPG jointly learn BS transmit beamforming, IRS phase shifts and the time-switching factor to maximize the harvested energy at the energy user.
system: p. 1: MISO; L-antenna BS, N-element passive reflecting IRS that harvests energy by time switching, M single-antenna information users, one single-antenna energy user; frequency band not stated.
method: p. 3: Deep reinforcement learning, DDPG actor-critic with two hidden layers; Double-DDPG uses two cooperating DDPG agents (beamforming and phases, time switching); trained online by interaction with the environment.
data_channel: p. 4: Channels randomly generated with Rayleigh distribution; path-loss exponents 2 (BS-IRS), 2.5 (IRS-users), 3.5 (BS-users); custom simulator, no dataset or measurement.
test_conditions: p. 4: Agents learn online in one simulated Rayleigh setting (M=4, N=40 for convergence); results swept over N=40 to 70 and M=2 to 5; no separate test scenario stated.
baselines: p. 4: DDPG (single agent), Fixed-SSF (DDPG, fixed time switching), Fixed-PS (random IRS phases, Double-DDPG for the rest; legend Fixed-PF), no-IRS system; no optimization-algorithm baseline.
metrics: p. 4: Episode and average reward (harvested energy at the EU, zero if constraints fail); harvested energy versus number of IRS elements N and of IUs M.
complexity: p. 4: Order of complexity as sums of layer-node products of actor and critic networks; O(D) < O(DD) < 2O(D) for DDPG versus Double-DDPG; no runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "following a Rayleigh distribution" - custom simulator with Rayleigh fading and fixed path-loss exponents; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 3: "layer neurons is decided by M, L and N" - network size follows M, L and N, so each value of N or M in the sweeps of Fig. 3 (p. 4) implies a separate agent; no test in an unseen scenario or after fine-tuning is reported.
q3_support: p. 4: "performance of the system compared to the DDPG algorithm" - standard DDPG applied to the same problem is the learned baseline; p. 4: "Θ is random" - Fixed-PS uses random IRS phases and no-IRS has no IRS, the non-learned references. Caveat: DDPG is also the paper's own single-agent design and Fixed-PS still learns beamforming and time switching.
q4_support: p. 4: "it is obvious that O(D) < O(DD) < 2O(D)" - complexity orders of DDPG and Double-DDPG given as sums of layer-node products of the actor and critic networks.
q5_support: p. 4: "We randomly generate the channel" - channels are simulated; no code or data link, no public channel dataset and no measured data are mentioned.
notes: Included, area 3: learned BS beamforming and IRS phase shifts (plus time switching) maximize the energy harvested at the EU, so the function is physical layer although the metric is energy. Borderline q3: the DDPG baseline is both a standard algorithm and the paper's own single-agent design; Fixed-PS keeps learned beamforming and time switching with random IRS phases; Fig. 3 legend says Fixed-PF while the text says Fixed-PS. No train/test split and no optimization (AO) baseline; CSI assumed known at the BS (p. 1).
